title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 69
paragraphs: Thus he spoke, and she answered him as follows: “My son, since you entreat me so earnestly to tell you the truth, the whole truth shall be told. When Ariston had brought me into his house, on the third night an apparition came to me in the likeness of Ariston; and after lying with me it placed upon me the garlands it was wearing and then went away. Soon afterward Ariston himself came. When he saw me wearing the garlands, he asked who had given them to me, and I said that he had. He denied it, but I began to swear to it, saying that he did wrong to deny it, for he had come only a short while before, lain with me, and given me the garlands. Then Ariston, seeing that I was taking an oath, realized that the matter was of the gods. And so indeed it was: the garlands were found to come from the hero-shrine that stands beside the outer door of our house — the shrine they call the temple of Astrabacus — and the diviners likewise answered that it was this very hero. So, my son, you now have the whole truth, as much as you wished to learn. You are begotten either of this hero — and Astrabacus is your father — or else of Ariston himself, for it was on that night that I conceived you. As for the point on which your enemies most eagerly seize — that Ariston, when your birth was announced, declared in the hearing of many that you were not his son, because the ten months had not yet been completed — he spoke that word out of ignorance of such matters. Women bring forth children at the ninth month as well, and even at the seventh, and not all after the full ten. I bore you, my son, at the seventh month; and Ariston himself before long recognized that he had uttered that saying in folly. Accept then no other reports about your birth; you have heard the entire truth. And as for Leotychides and all who spread such tales — may their own wives bear them children by keepers of asses!”
